summary: Iteration 12 verifies the new friendlier cookie-upload flow (cookies.txt auto-conversion + 3-step wizard with 'Test my session'). Backend: 19/19 new tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_social_session_upload.py covering parse_cookies_txt (tab parsing, #HttpOnly_, comment skip, bad-expiration fallback), normalise_session_upload (empty/garbage rejection with human message, storage_state dict / raw JSON array / Netscape text), POST /orgs/{id}/social/sessions in all three input shapes + regression on legacy storage_state, POST /orgs/{id}/social/sessions/{platform}/test with body.cookies_text (FAKE twitter cookies -> ok=False with 'couldn't confirm' message as specified) and with empty body -> falls back to persisted session. Regression suite test_social_autopost.py (10/10 fast tests, slow e2e skipped) also green. Frontend: logged in as the standing autopost-test account, verified (1) 'Manage login sessions' toggle opens panel, (2) 'Add a login session' launches the SessionWizard in a portal (visible over all other content, no click interception), (3) Step 1 renders a 2-column grid of all 7 supported platforms with label + domain, clicking X (Twitter) applies the orange highlight, Back button reads 'Cancel', (4) Step 2 shows the 3 numbered instructions, Chrome Web Store link points to cclelndahbckbenkjhflpdbgdldlbecc and the platform deep link is https://x.com/home (updates with platform), (5) Step 3 dropzone + hidden <details> paste textarea, pasting Netscape cookies populates raw + shows 'pasted 0.1 KB ready to upload' in emerald panel, (6) 'Test my session' calls /test, returns inline banner '⚠ Couldn't confirm you're logged in on Twitter — the page redirected to https://x.com/ without a members-only view…' exactly matching the heuristic spec, (7) Save button label dynamically switches to 'Save anyway' when the test fails, (8) Save persists via POST /social/sessions, wizard closes, and the session row appears with 'X / Twitter · TEST_wizard_twitter · 2 cookies' and a new 'Test' button alongside 'Delete'. Heuristic correctness confirmed end-to-end: fake-cookie session on x.com actually redirects to the marketing landing page and the backend's _PLATFORM_LOGGED_IN_PATHS check flips ok=False as designed.

issues: The 'paste instead' textarea lives inside a collapsed <details> element without any visible affordance on first load besides the summary caret. For non-technical users this is arguably perfect (dropzone is the happy path), but confirming the summary is labelled clearly — verified in code as 'Paste the cookies.txt contents or a storage_state JSON here'. No action needed; noting for future accessibility pass (the <summary> could use role='button' aria-expanded for screen readers).

critical_code_review_comments: social_autopost.py:75 parse_cookies_txt silently drops rows with <7 tab fields. That's correct for malformed rows, but when users paste space-separated (not tab) text nothing parses and normalise_session_upload falls through to the final ValueError. The error message DOES mention 'cookies.txt' and 'tab' is not explicitly called out — consider adding 'Make sure each line uses TAB characters between columns (not spaces).' to the format hint for extra user-friendliness. Low priority.

social_autopost.py:131 normalise_session_upload tries JSON first, then Netscape. If a user uploads `{}` (valid JSON but empty storage_state), _looks_like_storage_state returns False (no 'cookies' key with list value), and the function falls through to parse_cookies_txt which returns []. Final error is the format hint — correct behaviour, tested.

social_autopost.py:784 test_session accepts body=SessionTestBody(default_factory=SessionTestBody) so a bodiless POST with Content-Type:application/json and '{}' works — verified in test_empty_body_falls_back_to_persisted_session. Good.

social_autopost.py:755 cookies empty check 'if not cookies and not origins' lets origins-only uploads through (valid Playwright storage_state can have just origins). Edge case: a Netscape cookies.txt producing zero cookies but valid JSON shape would still 422 because parse_cookies_txt returns [] and the normalise_session_upload throws before this line. Logic is fine.

SocialPage.js:1196 SessionWizard correctly returns createPortal(..., document.body) — verified visually, modal sits above the underlying page and clicks on wizard-next are not intercepted (was reportedly a bug in E1's first attempt; the fix is correct).

SocialPage.js:1320-1340 drag-and-drop handlers use onDragOver/onDragLeave/onDrop with stopPropagation; the dropzone turns emerald (bg-emerald-500/10 text-emerald-200) when raw is populated — verified in screenshot.
SocialPage.js:1395 save button's `disabled={saving || !raw.trim()}` guards against empty submissions. Good UX — the button is inert until a cookie blob is present.

SessionWizard does NOT include a Close-on-ESC or click-outside-to-close handler — only the explicit X button and Cancel/Back chain close the portal. Not a bug, but a convention users often expect. Low priority enhancement.

The /test endpoint genuinely opens a headless Playwright browser and navigates to x.com — takes 15-40s per call and will always return ok=False for the fake cookies by design (marketing-page redirect heuristic). If this ever stops being slow, suspect that Playwright broke / isn't installed. Do NOT register a blanket page.on('dialog', lambda d: d.accept()) when testing the session-row Delete button in isolation — it will auto-accept the confirm() on both delete and alert popups; scope the handler or use page.once('dialog', ...).
rca of the issue: This iteration is a UX feature addition, not a bug fix, so no RCA. Change summary: (a) SocialSessionBody gained an optional cookies_text field alongside the existing optional storage_state — server-side parse_cookies_txt + normalise_session_upload handle the three input shapes transparently so non-technical users can drag-and-drop the raw Netscape file produced by Get-cookies.txt LOCALLY extension. (b) A new POST /orgs/{id}/social/sessions/{platform}/test endpoint headlessly navigates to a login-gated URL with the uploaded (or persisted) cookies and verifies redirect behaviour + DOM markers — it returns {ok, message, final_url}. (c) The React SessionWizard (createPortal into document.body) walks users through platform pick → extension install → file drop + test + save in 3 steps. Backward compat holds: sending the old {platform, storage_state} shape still works (legacy regression test passes).
